column1: # PRE-REGISTERED NUMERAL HITS — each one ruled by a non-author pane, with the receipt that ruled it.
# WHY A REGISTER RATHER THAN A FIX. `verify-reason-numerals.sh` reports every cited numeral it cannot
# open in the receipt cited for it. Three hits are live, and pane 3 ruled ALL THREE legitimate in form
# change, and a scope-narrowing are honest citations, not defects. A gate that went RED on them would
# be demanding that correct prose be rewritten to satisfy a substring match — which is why pane 3
# refused to wire this instrument for the whole session, and it was right to.
# So the gate does not check "zero hits". It checks "NO UNREGISTERED hits" — a ratchet. Every row here
# is a hit a pane examined and cleared, naming the receipt that carries the ruling. A new hit, or a
# changed numeral in an old one, is unregistered and turns the stage RED.
# HOW TO ADD A ROW, and the order is not negotiable: a non-author pane rules the hit first and writes
# a receipt, THEN the row cites that receipt. Adding a row to silence a gate — registering first and
# ruling later, or citing no receipt — is the exact laundering this file exists to prevent, and it is
# indistinguishable from an allowlist unless the ruling predates the row.
